title: Pressure ulcers: site, stage and healing
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's pressure ulcer, if any.
note:
Chief Complaint: Wound care for sacrum.

HPI: Pt is an 85-year-old female presenting for follow-up of a pressure ulcer located over the sacrum. Pt reports the area is uncomfortable but denies acute pain or drainage at this time. She notes she is using a pressure-redistributing mattress at home. No recent changes in mobility reported. Pt currently remains bedbound most of the day.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Meloxicam 15mg daily
- Acetaminophen 500mg PRN

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, or weight loss.
Integumentary: Positive for pressure ulcer on sacrum. No other skin concerns.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or weakness.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Lives at home with family support. Non-smoker. No alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had history of stroke.

Vitals:
BP: 138/84
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 96% on RA
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs:
HbA1c: 6.2%
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2
WBC: 8.2 (WNL)

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Skin: Pressure ulcer noted over the sacrum. Area is erythematous. No drainage noted. No purulent discharge. Remaining skin is intact and dry.
Respiratory: CTAB.
Cardiovascular: RRR, no murmurs.

Assessment:
1. Pressure ulcer of the sacrum.

Plan:
1. Wound care: Cleanse sacral area with normal saline. Apply thin layer of barrier cream.
2. Education: Reinforced importance of frequent repositioning and pressure-relieving surfaces.
3. Follow up: Return to clinic in 2 weeks for wound assessment.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, DO
05/12/2026
explanations: Pressure ulcer of the sacral region, stage not documented: L89.159 (no HCC).

distractors.why: No stage is documented: use the unspecified-stage code.
